summary: Opaque 429 spikes during nightly parallel backfill with websocket preflight double-counting
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429s during their nightly parallel backfill (bulk sync) which runs from 02:00-04:00 in us-west. The backfill uses multiplexed websocket sessions for control and short-lived signed callbacks for per-object completion. Spikes started after the customer scaled their orchestrator from 50 -> 200 parallel workers.

Impact:
- ~18% of backfill jobs observed 429s and retry storms leading to >10% longer completion time for the night run.
- Errors are limited to the dedicated tenant; interactive traffic (low-latency chat) unaffected.

Environment:
- Redwood dedicated pool (prod - us-west)
- Customer: Voltique Analytics (dedicated)
- Orchestrator: custom multi-process worker that opens multiplexed websockets + signed-url callbacks per completed file
- Affected model: redwood-7b-quantized

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Schedule a parallel backfill with 150+ workers concurrently uploading via the same tenant API key.
2) Each worker opens a short-lived websocket control connection and periodically issues preflight POSTs to /v1/uploads/preflight followed by signed-url callbacks to /v1/uploads/callback.
3) Observe 429s starting ~30 minutes into the run; they appear in waves every 10s-12s.

Expected behavior:
- Backfill should proceed without tenant-scoped throttling when below committed dedicated throughput.

Actual behavior:
- Tenant receives opaque 429 responses for upload endpoints. Throttles appear correlated to the preflight/callback pattern and to the number of simultaneous websocket control connections.

Logs / traces attached by customer (excerpt):
- "2026-03-11T02:37:12Z 429 /v1/uploads/preflight tenant_id=voltique-worker-17 conn_id=ws-4312"
- Health-checks and low-latency chat routes show normal success rates.

Notes from the customer:
- Rotating short-lived keys per worker to improve security; each worker registers a signed callback that completes within ~3s of the upload finishing.
- Problem began after scaling workers and after enabling a fronting CDN/edge rewrite that normalizes upload urls to /v1/uploads/*

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Suggest pacing backfill workers or reducing concurrent websocket connections. Customer tried ramping to 50 workers and saw the issue stop.
